# Jiro: full text

> Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori. It runs Claude Code or Codex in isolated cloud VMs on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription or API key, or Cursor with a Cursor API key, works from Slack and the web, and opens pull requests on your GitHub repos for review.

# Amp alternatives (2026): coding agents compared after the orbs relaunch

Updated 2026-10-17

> **What are the best alternatives to Amp (ampcode)?**
>
> Jiro is the best Amp alternative for teams that want an agent working in Slack and opening pull requests for review, rather than pushing to trunk by default: it runs Claude Code or Codex in its own cloud VMs on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori. Claude Code on the web, Cursor cloud agents, Codex cloud, Tembo and OpenHands are the other options.

## Amp and the alternatives at a glance

|  | Runs where | Models and keys | Start work from | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jiro | An isolated cloud VM per conversation, with your repos and setup script | Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription or API key; Cursor with a Cursor API key | Slack, web chat, your own cron and webhook automations | 30-day free trial, no card; billed per runtime, not per token |
| Amp | Amp cloud orbs or your own runners [1] | Own subscriptions and keys, no BYOK fee [2] | Web, macOS/iOS, CLI, GitHub, Slack [3] | Hobby free; Megawatt $20/mo; Gigawatt $200/mo [4] |
| Claude Code on the web | Anthropic-managed VMs [5] | Claude models; Anthropic account required [6] | Web, mobile, desktop, terminal [7] | In Pro $20/mo, Max $100+/mo, Team seats [8] |
| Cursor cloud agents | Cursor cloud VMs or self-hosted workers [9] | Billed at API prices for the chosen model; own keys chat-only [10] | Desktop, web, mobile, Slack, Teams, GitHub, Linear, API [11] | Premium $30/mo+ (X Subscription) plus API-priced usage [12] |
| Codex cloud | OpenAI-hosted VMs [13] | OpenAI models; cloud needs a ChatGPT plan [14] | ChatGPT apps, CLI, IDE, Slack, GitHub, Linear [15] | In ChatGPT Plus $20/mo and up [16] |
| Tembo | Tembo cloud sessions [17] | Multiple harnesses; own keys or subscriptions [18] | GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, Sentry, schedules [19] | Pro $60/mo; Max $200/mo; compute per second [20] |
| OpenHands | Local, OpenHands cloud, or self-hosted [21] | Own agent or popular CLIs; your keys [22] | GUI, CLI, API, GitHub, Slack, Jira [23] | Free (10 conversations/day hosted); Enterprise custom [24] |

## Amp after its 2026 rebuild

Amp changed a lot this year. Amp retired its VS Code and Cursor extensions in February 2026. [25] Cloud work moved to orbs, billed by the minute. Orbs are billed per minute, from $0.08 an hour for the smallest size. [26]

It is also generous on bringing your own models. Amp accepts ChatGPT, Claude Pro or Max and other subscriptions as well as API keys, and charges no token fees on your own keys outside its Enterprise tier. [2] Amp added Claude Pro and Max subscription support through the Claude Agent SDK on 2026-10-10. [27] The catch for teams is the default workflow: Amp's default Ship pushes straight to the base branch after tests; the Push to Branch setting opens a pull request instead. [28]

## The alternatives, ranked

Ranked for teams that want reviewable pull requests and a shared place to ask for work.

### 1. Jiro: best for team review workflows

Jiro opens pull requests for review on your GitHub repos and asks before merging to your main branch, so its work goes through the same review and branch protection as everyone else's.

Each conversation gets an isolated cloud VM with your repos and setup script. Jiro runs Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription, an API key or OpenRouter, or Cursor with a Cursor API key, and bills for the runtime rather than the tokens. Your team works with it in Slack or the web chat.

**Pick Jiro if** you like Amp's bring-your-own-model approach but want a PR-first team workflow.

### 2. Claude Code on the web: best for solo Claude subscribers

A Claude Code cloud session runs on Anthropic-managed infrastructure (by default a 4 vCPU, 16 GB VM) and keeps running after you close your laptop. [5] Claude Code is included in Claude Pro ($20 a month), Max (from $100 a month) and Team and Enterprise seats, with no separate charge for the cloud VM; the Free plan has no Claude Code. [8]

**Pick it if** you mostly want Claude Code on your own laptop and phone.

### 3. Cursor cloud agents: best for Cursor users

Cursor cloud agents run in isolated cloud VMs with full development environments, or on self-hosted workers while Cursor runs the agent loop. [9] Cursor cloud agents produce merge-ready PRs with screenshots, videos and logs, and open a PR in each repo they touch. [29]

**Pick Cursor if** you miss having the agent in your editor.

### 4. OpenAI Codex cloud: best for ChatGPT teams

Codex cloud runs each task in an OpenAI-hosted VM and keeps working while your laptop sleeps. [13] Codex cloud is included from ChatGPT Plus at $20 a month; Pro costs $100 to $500 a month and Business $25 per user monthly, with usage limits shared with ChatGPT. [16]

**Pick Codex cloud if** a ChatGPT plan covers everyone.

### 5. Tembo: best for multi-harness orchestration

Tembo runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Amp or OpenCode per task and accepts your own API keys or a Claude, ChatGPT or SuperGrok subscription. [18] Tembo's Pro plan is $60 a month and Max $200 a month, each including a usage allowance, with compute billed per second from $0.1066 an hour. [20]

**Pick Tembo if** you want event-driven agents across many tools.

### 6. OpenHands: best open-source option

OpenHands is an MIT-licensed open-source platform for software engineering agents. [30] OpenHands' hosted Individual tier is free for one user with 10 conversations a day; local use is free and Enterprise is custom. [24]

**Pick OpenHands if** you want to run the agent yourself.

## When Amp is the better fit

Stay with Amp if you work trunk-based, want to choose machine sizes per thread, or want a fully free setup on your own compute and keys.

## FAQ

### What is the best alternative to Amp?

For teams that review every change, Jiro: it opens pull requests and runs Claude Code or Codex in cloud VMs on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription. For solo Claude users, Claude Code on the web.

### Is Amp still ad-supported?

No. Amp removed ads from its free tier on 2026-03-30. [31] The free path is now its Hobby tier with your own keys or compute.

### Does Amp have a VS Code extension?

Not anymore. Amp retired its VS Code and Cursor extensions in February 2026. [25]

### Is Jiro related to Amp or Sourcegraph?

No. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori, an independent company.

## Try Jiro

Start the 30-day free trial, no card needed: https://login.norisessions.com/?signup=1&entrypoint=jiro

Or install Jiro's engineering skills into your own agent: `npx nori-skillsets install public/jiro`

# Claude Code on the web alternatives (2026): cloud Claude Code for teams

Updated 2026-10-17

> **What are the best alternatives to Claude Code on the web?**
>
> Jiro is the best alternative to Claude Code on the web for teams: it runs Anthropic's Claude Code in its own cloud VMs on your own Claude subscription or API key, and your team works with it in Slack. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori. Codex cloud, Cursor cloud agents, Amp, Tembo and Copilot cloud agent are the other options.

## Claude Code on the web and the alternatives at a glance

|  | Runs where | Models and keys | Start work from | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jiro | An isolated cloud VM per conversation, with your repos and setup script | Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription or API key; Cursor with a Cursor API key | Slack, web chat, your own cron and webhook automations | 30-day free trial, no card; billed per runtime, not per token |
| Claude Code on the web | Anthropic-managed VMs [1] | Claude models; Anthropic account required [2] | Web, mobile, desktop, terminal [3] | In Pro $20/mo, Max $100+/mo, Team seats [4] |
| Codex cloud | OpenAI-hosted VMs [5] | OpenAI models; cloud needs a ChatGPT plan [6] | ChatGPT apps, CLI, IDE, Slack, GitHub, Linear [7] | In ChatGPT Plus $20/mo and up [8] |
| Cursor cloud agents | Cursor cloud VMs or self-hosted workers [9] | Billed at API prices for the chosen model; own keys chat-only [10] | Desktop, web, mobile, Slack, Teams, GitHub, Linear, API [11] | Premium $30/mo+ (X Subscription) plus API-priced usage [12] |
| Amp | Amp cloud orbs or your own runners [13] | Own subscriptions and keys, no BYOK fee [14] | Web, macOS/iOS, CLI, GitHub, Slack [15] | Hobby free; Megawatt $20/mo; Gigawatt $200/mo [16] |
| Tembo | Tembo cloud sessions [17] | Multiple harnesses; own keys or subscriptions [18] | GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, Sentry, schedules [19] | Pro $60/mo; Max $200/mo; compute per second [20] |
| Copilot cloud agent | GitHub Actions runners, 59-minute sessions [21] | Many models via GitHub; own keys not documented for it [22] | GitHub, IDEs, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [23] | Pro $10; Pro+ $39; Max $100; Business $19/user [24] |

## What Claude Code on the web is good at

A Claude Code cloud session runs on Anthropic-managed infrastructure (by default a 4 vCPU, 16 GB VM) and keeps running after you close your laptop. [1] Cloud sessions start from claude.ai/code, the Claude mobile and desktop apps, and `claude --cloud` in a terminal, and `claude --teleport` pulls a session back to your machine. [3] For a single developer on a Claude plan, it is the most direct way to run Claude Code in the cloud. Claude Code is included in Claude Pro ($20 a month), Max (from $100 a month) and Team and Enterprise seats, with no separate charge for the cloud VM; the Free plan has no Claude Code. [4]

Teams hit two things. Slack is changing. For Team and Enterprise, Slack work moves to Claude Tag (public beta), and the legacy Claude Code Slack bot was retired on 2026-10-05 in workspaces connected to a Claude organization. [25] Claude Tag bills Slack channel work by usage under an admin-set spend limit. [26] And it is Claude-only by design. Cloud sessions run Claude models and require an Anthropic account; they are not available through Bedrock, Google Cloud or other third-party providers. [2]

## The alternatives, ranked

Ranked for teams that want Claude Code working in the background for everyone, not one laptop at a time.

### 1. Jiro: Claude Code in the cloud, for the whole team

Jiro runs Anthropic's Claude Code in an isolated cloud VM with your GitHub repos and setup script, signed in with your own Claude subscription or an API key.

Your team mentions Jiro in Slack or uses the web chat; Jiro replies in the thread and opens pull requests for review. When a task suits Codex or Cursor better, connect that provider and start a new conversation with it. It asks before merging to your main branch.

**Pick Jiro if** you want Claude Code working in your team's Slack on credentials you control.

### 2. OpenAI Codex cloud: the OpenAI counterpart

Codex cloud runs each task in an OpenAI-hosted VM and keeps working while your laptop sleeps. [5] Codex cloud is included from ChatGPT Plus at $20 a month; Pro costs $100 to $500 a month and Business $25 per user monthly, with usage limits shared with ChatGPT. [8]

**Pick Codex cloud if** your team prefers OpenAI models.

### 3. Cursor cloud agents: best for Cursor users

Cursor cloud agents produce merge-ready PRs with screenshots, videos and logs, and open a PR in each repo they touch. [27] Cursor is sold as part of The X Subscription; cloud agents need the Premium tier ($30 a month) or higher, and third-party models are billed from prepaid credit at API list price. [12]

**Pick Cursor if** your developers work in the Cursor editor.

### 4. Amp: best bring-your-own-everything option

Amp accepts ChatGPT, Claude Pro or Max and other subscriptions as well as API keys, and charges no token fees on your own keys outside its Enterprise tier. [14] Amp added Claude Pro and Max subscription support through the Claude Agent SDK on 2026-10-10. [28] Amp runs cloud work in orbs, one remote machine per thread that keeps working while your laptop is closed, or on your own machines as runners. [13]

**Pick Amp if** you want per-minute cloud machines or a free path on your own hardware.

### 5. Tembo: best for alert-driven work

Tembo runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Amp or OpenCode per task and accepts your own API keys or a Claude, ChatGPT or SuperGrok subscription. [18] Tembo starts work from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Slack, Linear, Jira, Sentry, PagerDuty, webhooks and schedules. [19]

**Pick Tembo if** most agent work should start from Sentry, PagerDuty or ticket events.

### 6. GitHub Copilot cloud agent: best inside GitHub

On Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise, Claude and Codex can be assigned GitHub tasks as third-party agents (public preview). [29] Copilot cloud agent opens draft pull requests on its own branch and cannot approve or merge them. [30]

**Pick Copilot if** you want GitHub to run Claude as one of several agents.

## When to stay with Claude Code on the web

Stay with it if you work alone, want to move one session between web, phone, desktop and terminal, and only need Claude models. Anthropic does not charge extra for the cloud VM.

## FAQ

### Can I run Claude Code in the cloud with my Claude Max subscription?

Yes, with Claude Code on the web. Jiro also runs Claude Code in its cloud VMs on your own Claude subscription or API key.

### How do I run Claude Code in Slack for my team?

Connect Jiro to Slack, GitHub and a Claude subscription or Anthropic API key, then mention Jiro in a channel. It works in a cloud VM and replies in the thread with a pull request when code changes.

### Is Jiro made by Anthropic?

No. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori. It runs Anthropic's Claude Code, as well as Codex and Cursor.

### Is Claude Code on the web free?

No. Claude Code is included in Claude Pro ($20 a month), Max (from $100 a month) and Team and Enterprise seats, with no separate charge for the cloud VM; the Free plan has no Claude Code. [4]

## Try Jiro

Start the 30-day free trial, no card needed: https://login.norisessions.com/?signup=1&entrypoint=jiro

Or install Jiro's engineering skills into your own agent: `npx nori-skillsets install public/jiro`

# OpenAI Codex cloud alternatives (2026)

Updated 2026-10-17

> **What are the best alternatives to OpenAI Codex cloud?**
>
> Jiro is the best Codex cloud alternative for teams that want more than OpenAI models: it runs Codex or Claude Code in its own cloud VMs on your ChatGPT or Claude subscription, and Cursor on a Cursor API key. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori. Claude Code on the web, Cursor cloud agents, Copilot cloud agent, Jules and Devin are the other options.

## Codex cloud and the alternatives at a glance

|  | Runs where | Models and keys | Start work from | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jiro | An isolated cloud VM per conversation, with your repos and setup script | Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription or API key; Cursor with a Cursor API key | Slack, web chat, your own cron and webhook automations | 30-day free trial, no card; billed per runtime, not per token |
| Codex cloud | OpenAI-hosted VMs [1] | OpenAI models; cloud needs a ChatGPT plan [2] | ChatGPT apps, CLI, IDE, Slack, GitHub, Linear [3] | In ChatGPT Plus $20/mo and up [4] |
| Claude Code on the web | Anthropic-managed VMs [5] | Claude models; Anthropic account required [6] | Web, mobile, desktop, terminal [7] | In Pro $20/mo, Max $100+/mo, Team seats [8] |
| Cursor cloud agents | Cursor cloud VMs or self-hosted workers [9] | Billed at API prices for the chosen model; own keys chat-only [10] | Desktop, web, mobile, Slack, Teams, GitHub, Linear, API [11] | Premium $30/mo+ (X Subscription) plus API-priced usage [12] |
| Copilot cloud agent | GitHub Actions runners, 59-minute sessions [13] | Many models via GitHub; own keys not documented for it [14] | GitHub, IDEs, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [15] | Pro $10; Pro+ $39; Max $100; Business $19/user [16] |
| Jules | Google-hosted short-lived VMs [17] | Gemini only [18] | Web, GitHub label, CLI, API [19] | Free; AI Pro $19.99/mo; Ultra from $99.99/mo [20] |
| Devin | Cognition cloud VMs, or local [21] | Multi-vendor, Cognition-routed; ChatGPT plan linking on paid plans [22] | Web, desktop, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [23] | Free; Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams $80/mo + $40/seat; overage at API prices [24] |

## Codex cloud today

Codex cloud runs each task in an OpenAI-hosted VM and keeps working while your laptop sleeps. [1] Codex cloud is included from ChatGPT Plus at $20 a month; Pro costs $100 to $500 a month and Business $25 per user monthly, with usage limits shared with ChatGPT. [4] For anyone already paying for ChatGPT, that bundle is hard to beat on price.

Two things push teams to look around. First, it is OpenAI-only: Codex cloud runs OpenAI models; an API key unlocks Codex in the CLI, SDK and IDE but not cloud features, which need a ChatGPT plan. [2] Second, the integrations are mid-migration: Codex requests in Slack now start with @ChatGPT instead of @Codex. [25] Codex Cloud (Legacy) still powers Code Review and the GitHub and Linear integrations, and OpenAI plans to deprecate it. [26]

## The alternatives, ranked

Ranked for teams that want a cloud coding agent beyond a single model vendor.

### 1. Jiro: keep Codex, add Claude Code and Cursor

You do not have to give up Codex to switch. Jiro runs Codex as one of its agents, on your ChatGPT subscription or API key, in a cloud VM with your GitHub repos and setup script. When Claude Code or Cursor suits a task better, connect that provider and start a new conversation with it.

Jiro opens pull requests for review and asks before merging to your main branch.

**Pick Jiro if** you want Codex in the cloud without being limited to OpenAI's models and integrations.

### 2. Claude Code on the web: the Anthropic equivalent

A Claude Code cloud session runs on Anthropic-managed infrastructure (by default a 4 vCPU, 16 GB VM) and keeps running after you close your laptop. [5] Claude Code is included in Claude Pro ($20 a month), Max (from $100 a month) and Team and Enterprise seats, with no separate charge for the cloud VM; the Free plan has no Claude Code. [8]

**Pick it if** you prefer Claude models and work mostly alone. Cloud sessions run Claude models and require an Anthropic account; they are not available through Bedrock, Google Cloud or other third-party providers. [6]

### 3. Cursor cloud agents: best in the editor

Cursor cloud agents run in isolated cloud VMs with full development environments, or on self-hosted workers while Cursor runs the agent loop. [9] Cursor is sold as part of The X Subscription; cloud agents need the Premium tier ($30 a month) or higher, and third-party models are billed from prepaid credit at API list price. [12]

**Pick Cursor if** your team works in Cursor already.

### 4. GitHub Copilot cloud agent: best inside GitHub

GitHub's Copilot cloud agent, formerly the Copilot coding agent, researches a repository, plans changes and implements them in an ephemeral environment powered by GitHub Actions. [27] On Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise, Claude and Codex can be assigned GitHub tasks as third-party agents (public preview). [28]

**Pick Copilot if** you want GitHub to orchestrate several agents, including Codex.

### 5. Jules: best free tier

Jules allows 15 tasks a day and 3 at once on the free tier, 100 a day and 15 at once with Google AI Pro, and 300 a day and 60 at once with AI Ultra. [29]

**Pick Jules if** you want to try a cloud agent at no cost on a personal account.

### 6. Devin: best fully managed option

Cognition describes Devin as an autonomous software engineer that runs in the cloud or on your machine and tests its work in its own browser. [30] Devin uses models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google plus Cognition's own SWE models, picked by an Adaptive router; Pro, Max and Teams users can link a ChatGPT plan for the GPT share of usage. [22]

**Pick Devin if** you want one vendor for agent, models and integrations.

## When Codex cloud is enough

Stay with Codex cloud if everyone on the team has a ChatGPT plan, OpenAI models cover your work, and you start tasks from ChatGPT or the CLI.

## FAQ

### What is the best alternative to OpenAI Codex cloud?

Jiro, if you want Codex plus Claude Code and Cursor in one place on your own subscriptions. Claude Code on the web if you want Anthropic's equivalent.

### Can I use my ChatGPT subscription with Jiro?

Yes. Jiro's setup accepts a ChatGPT subscription through device-code sign-in, or an OpenAI API key, and runs Codex with it.

### Does Codex cloud work with an API key?

Only partly. Codex cloud runs OpenAI models; an API key unlocks Codex in the CLI, SDK and IDE but not cloud features, which need a ChatGPT plan. [2]

### Is Jiro built on Codex?

No. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori that can run Codex, Claude Code or Cursor as the underlying agent.

## Try Jiro

Start the 30-day free trial, no card needed: https://login.norisessions.com/?signup=1&entrypoint=jiro

Or install Jiro's engineering skills into your own agent: `npx nori-skillsets install public/jiro`

# GitHub Copilot coding agent alternatives (2026)

Updated 2026-10-17

> **What are the best alternatives to GitHub Copilot coding agent?**
>
> The best GitHub Copilot coding agent alternatives are Jiro, OpenAI Codex cloud, Cursor cloud agents, Claude Code on the web, Devin and OpenHands, and Jiro is the top pick when work starts in Slack rather than GitHub issues, because it gives each conversation its own cloud VM and runs Claude Code, Codex or Cursor on your own subscription. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori.

## Copilot cloud agent and the alternatives at a glance

|  | Runs where | Models and keys | Start work from | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jiro | An isolated cloud VM per conversation, with your repos and setup script | Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription or API key; Cursor with a Cursor API key | Slack, web chat, your own cron and webhook automations | 30-day free trial, no card; billed per runtime, not per token |
| Copilot cloud agent | GitHub Actions runners, 59-minute sessions [1] | Many models via GitHub; own keys not documented for it [2] | GitHub, IDEs, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [3] | Pro $10; Pro+ $39; Max $100; Business $19/user [4] |
| Codex cloud | OpenAI-hosted VMs [5] | OpenAI models; cloud needs a ChatGPT plan [6] | ChatGPT apps, CLI, IDE, Slack, GitHub, Linear [7] | In ChatGPT Plus $20/mo and up [8] |
| Cursor cloud agents | Cursor cloud VMs or self-hosted workers [9] | Billed at API prices for the chosen model; own keys chat-only [10] | Desktop, web, mobile, Slack, Teams, GitHub, Linear, API [11] | Premium $30/mo+ (X Subscription) plus API-priced usage [12] |

| OpenHands | Local, OpenHands cloud, or self-hosted [21] | Own agent or popular CLIs; your keys [22] | GUI, CLI, API, GitHub, Slack, Jira [23] | Free (10 conversations/day hosted); Enterprise custom [24] |

## Copilot's agent after the rename

GitHub's Copilot cloud agent, formerly the Copilot coding agent, researches a repository, plans changes and implements them in an ephemeral environment powered by GitHub Actions. [25] Its guardrails are the best defaults in the category: Copilot cloud agent opens draft pull requests on its own branch and cannot approve or merge them. [26]

The constraints come from running on Actions. Copilot cloud agent sessions run on GitHub Actions runners, for at most 59 minutes each, on GitHub-hosted repositories. [1] Billing also changed this year. Since 2026-06-01, Copilot usage is billed in GitHub AI Credits metered by tokens. [27] On models: The cloud agent offers Auto plus Claude, Gemini, GPT and Grok models; bring-your-own-key is documented for Copilot Chat, CLI and IDEs, not for the cloud agent. [2]

## The alternatives, ranked

Ranked for teams whose work does not always start as a GitHub issue.

### 1. Jiro: best when the work starts in Slack

Mention Jiro in Slack or open the web chat, and it picks the work up in a cloud VM with your GitHub repos and setup script.

It runs Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription or API key, or Cursor on your Cursor key, opens pull requests for review, and asks before merging to your main branch. Your branch protection rules still apply to its PRs.

**Pick Jiro if** you want a teammate you can talk to, not only an issue assignee.

### 2. OpenAI Codex cloud: best for ChatGPT teams

Codex cloud runs each task in an OpenAI-hosted VM and keeps working while your laptop sleeps. [5] Codex cloud is included from ChatGPT Plus at $20 a month; Pro costs $100 to $500 a month and Business $25 per user monthly, with usage limits shared with ChatGPT. [8]

**Pick Codex cloud if** you want long-running cloud tasks on a ChatGPT plan.

### 3. Cursor cloud agents: best for editor-first teams

Cursor cloud agents run in isolated cloud VMs with full development environments, or on self-hosted workers while Cursor runs the agent loop. [9] Cursor cloud agents produce merge-ready PRs with screenshots, videos and logs, and open a PR in each repo they touch. [28]

**Pick Cursor if** you need GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps support. Cloud agents start from the Cursor desktop app, the web, iOS, Slack, Microsoft Teams, GitHub and Bitbucket comments, Linear and an API, on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps repos. [11]

### 4. Claude Code on the web: best for Claude subscribers

A Claude Code cloud session runs on Anthropic-managed infrastructure (by default a 4 vCPU, 16 GB VM) and keeps running after you close your laptop. [13] Cloud sessions push a branch; you review the diff and create the pull request, and auto-fix can then push fixes for CI failures and review comments. [29]

**Pick it if** you already pay for Claude Pro or Max and work mostly alone.

### 5. Devin: best for broad enterprise integrations

Devin works from its web app, Devin Desktop, the Devin CLI, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Linear and Jira, with GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket repos. [19] Devin's self-serve plans are Free, Pro at $20 a month, Max at $200 a month and Teams at an $80 monthly minimum plus $40 per seat; usage beyond the quota is billed at API pricing, and Enterprise is billed in ACUs. [20]

**Pick Devin if** you need Jira, Teams and multiple code hosts from a managed service.

### 6. OpenHands: best open-source option

OpenHands is an MIT-licensed open-source platform for software engineering agents. [30] Labelling a GitHub issue openhands or commenting @openhands starts a run that opens a PR if it resolves the issue. [31]

**Pick OpenHands if** you like Copilot's label-an-issue flow but want to self-host.

## When to stay with Copilot

Stay with Copilot if your organisation already pays for Copilot Business or Enterprise, tasks fit in one session, and you want the agent to live entirely inside GitHub. It can also hand tasks to Claude and Codex. On Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise, Claude and Codex can be assigned GitHub tasks as third-party agents (public preview). [32]

## FAQ

### Is GitHub Copilot coding agent the same as Copilot cloud agent?

Yes. GitHub's Copilot cloud agent, formerly the Copilot coding agent, researches a repository, plans changes and implements them in an ephemeral environment powered by GitHub Actions. [25]

### When should I pick Copilot over Jiro?

When your organisation already pays for Copilot, work starts as GitHub issues, and tasks fit in one Actions session. Pick Jiro when work starts in Slack or you want to use your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription.

### Can I use my own model subscription instead of Copilot credits?

Yes with Jiro, which runs Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription, an API key or OpenRouter, or Cursor with a Cursor API key.

### Does Jiro work with GitHub branch protection?

Yes. Jiro works through pull requests on your GitHub repos, so your branch protection and required checks apply to its changes.

Start the 30-day free trial, no card needed: https://login.norisessions.com/?signup=1&entrypoint=jiro

Or install Jiro's engineering skills into your own agent: `npx nori-skillsets install public/jiro`

# Cursor background agents alternatives (2026): now called Cloud Agents

Updated 2026-10-17

> **What are the best alternatives to Cursor background agents?**
>
> The best alternatives to Cursor background agents are Jiro, OpenAI Codex cloud, GitHub Copilot cloud agent, Claude Code on the web, Devin and Amp, and Jiro is the top pick if you want Claude Code or Codex in the cloud on the Claude or ChatGPT subscription you already pay for, with Cursor's own agent available on your Cursor API key. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori.

## Cursor cloud agents and the alternatives at a glance

|  | Runs where | Models and keys | Start work from | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jiro | An isolated cloud VM per conversation, with your repos and setup script | Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription or API key; Cursor with a Cursor API key | Slack, web chat, your own cron and webhook automations | 30-day free trial, no card; billed per runtime, not per token |
| Cursor cloud agents | Cursor cloud VMs or self-hosted workers [1] | Billed at API prices for the chosen model; own keys chat-only [2] | Desktop, web, mobile, Slack, Teams, GitHub, Linear, API [3] | Premium $30/mo+ (X Subscription) plus API-priced usage [4] |
| Codex cloud | OpenAI-hosted VMs [5] | OpenAI models; cloud needs a ChatGPT plan [6] | ChatGPT apps, CLI, IDE, Slack, GitHub, Linear [7] | In ChatGPT Plus $20/mo and up [8] |
| Copilot cloud agent | GitHub Actions runners, 59-minute sessions [9] | Many models via GitHub; own keys not documented for it [10] | GitHub, IDEs, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [11] | Pro $10; Pro+ $39; Max $100; Business $19/user [12] |
| Claude Code on the web | Anthropic-managed VMs [13] | Claude models; Anthropic account required [14] | Web, mobile, desktop, terminal [15] | In Pro $20/mo, Max $100+/mo, Team seats [16] |
| Devin | Cognition cloud VMs, or local [17] | Multi-vendor, Cognition-routed; ChatGPT plan linking on paid plans [18] | Web, desktop, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [19] | Free; Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams $80/mo + $40/seat; overage at API prices [20] |
| Amp | Amp cloud orbs or your own runners [21] | Own subscriptions and keys, no BYOK fee [22] | Web, macOS/iOS, CLI, GitHub, Slack [23] | Hobby free; Megawatt $20/mo; Gigawatt $200/mo [24] |

## What changed with Cursor's background agents

Cursor now calls its background agents Cloud Agents. [25] Cursor cloud agents run in isolated cloud VMs with full development environments, or on self-hosted workers while Cursor runs the agent loop. [1] The product is strong: Cursor cloud agents produce merge-ready PRs with screenshots, videos and logs, and open a PR in each repo they touch. [26]

Pricing has changed: Cursor is sold as part of The X Subscription; cloud agents need the Premium tier ($30 a month) or higher, and third-party models are billed from prepaid credit at API list price. [4] Customers on Cursor's legacy Pro, Pro+ and Teams plans can keep them; switching to the new plans is optional but permanent. [27] On usage, Cursor's docs say: Cloud agents are charged at API pricing for the selected model, and Cursor's custom API keys only work with chat models. [2]

## The alternatives, ranked

Ranked for teams that liked Cursor's background agents but want a different billing model or a different home for the work.

### 1. Jiro: best if you want your own subscription in the cloud

Jiro runs the agent harness you pick in an isolated cloud VM with your GitHub repos and setup script: Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription, an API key or OpenRouter, or Cursor's agent on your Cursor API key. Jiro bills for the runtime rather than the tokens.

Your team works with it in Slack or the web chat, and it opens pull requests for review. It asks before merging anything to your main branch.

**Pick Jiro if** you want cloud agents on the Claude or ChatGPT plan you already have.

### 2. OpenAI Codex cloud: best for ChatGPT teams

Codex cloud runs each task in an OpenAI-hosted VM and keeps working while your laptop sleeps. [5] Codex cloud is included from ChatGPT Plus at $20 a month; Pro costs $100 to $500 a month and Business $25 per user monthly, with usage limits shared with ChatGPT. [8]

**Pick Codex cloud if** OpenAI models are all you need.

### 3. GitHub Copilot cloud agent: best for GitHub-centred teams

GitHub's Copilot cloud agent, formerly the Copilot coding agent, researches a repository, plans changes and implements them in an ephemeral environment powered by GitHub Actions. [28] Copilot cloud agent opens draft pull requests on its own branch and cannot approve or merge them. [29]

**Pick Copilot if** your work starts as GitHub issues. Since 2026-06-01, Copilot usage is billed in GitHub AI Credits metered by tokens. [30]

### 4. Claude Code on the web: best for individual Claude subscribers

A Claude Code cloud session runs on Anthropic-managed infrastructure (by default a 4 vCPU, 16 GB VM) and keeps running after you close your laptop. [13] Claude Code is included in Claude Pro ($20 a month), Max (from $100 a month) and Team and Enterprise seats, with no separate charge for the cloud VM; the Free plan has no Claude Code. [16]

**Pick Claude Code on the web if** you work alone or mostly from your own laptop and phone. For team Slack use, Anthropic is moving to Claude Tag. For Team and Enterprise, Slack work moves to Claude Tag (public beta), and the legacy Claude Code Slack bot was retired on 2026-10-05 in workspaces connected to a Claude organization. [31]

### 5. Devin: best managed, broad-integration option

Cognition describes Devin as an autonomous software engineer that runs in the cloud or on your machine and tests its work in its own browser. [32] Devin's self-serve plans are Free, Pro at $20 a month, Max at $200 a month and Teams at an $80 monthly minimum plus $40 per seat; usage beyond the quota is billed at API pricing, and Enterprise is billed in ACUs. [20]

**Pick Devin if** you want Teams, Jira and GitLab support from one vendor.

### 6. Amp: best for tinkerers who bring their own compute

Amp runs cloud work in orbs, one remote machine per thread that keeps working while your laptop is closed, or on your own machines as runners. [21] Amp accepts ChatGPT, Claude Pro or Max and other subscriptions as well as API keys, and charges no token fees on your own keys outside its Enterprise tier. [22]

**Pick Amp if** you want per-minute cloud machines and a fully free path on your own hardware. Note that by default it pushes straight to your base branch. Amp's default Ship pushes straight to the base branch after tests; the Push to Branch setting opens a pull request instead. [33]

## When to stay with Cursor

Stay with Cursor if your developers live in the editor, want the agent in the same tool, or your repos live on GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps. Cloud agents start from the Cursor desktop app, the web, iOS, Slack, Microsoft Teams, GitHub and Bitbucket comments, Linear and an API, on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps repos. [3]

## FAQ

### Are Cursor background agents and Cursor cloud agents the same thing?

Yes. Cursor now calls its background agents Cloud Agents. [25]

### Can Jiro run Cursor's agent?

Yes. Cursor is one of the agents Jiro can run in its cloud VMs, alongside Claude Code and Codex. Cursor needs your Cursor API key; Claude Code and Codex use your Claude or ChatGPT credentials.

### What is the best Cursor background agents alternative for Slack?

Jiro is built around Slack: mention it in a channel and it replies in the thread and opens pull requests. Cursor, Codex and Copilot also take requests from Slack.

### Is Jiro a code editor?

No. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori. It works in cloud VMs and returns pull requests; you keep your editor.

## Try Jiro

Start the 30-day free trial, no card needed: https://login.norisessions.com/?signup=1&entrypoint=jiro

Or install Jiro's engineering skills into your own agent: `npx nori-skillsets install public/jiro`

# Devin alternatives (2026): background coding agents compared

Updated 2026-10-17

> **What are the best Devin alternatives?**
>
> The best Devin alternative for most teams is Jiro, because it runs Claude Code or Codex in its own cloud VMs on the Claude or ChatGPT subscription you already pay for, instead of a separate usage quota. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori. Other strong options are OpenAI Codex cloud, Cursor cloud agents, GitHub Copilot cloud agent, Google Jules and the open-source OpenHands.

## Devin and its alternatives at a glance

|  | Runs where | Models and keys | Start work from | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jiro | An isolated cloud VM per conversation, with your repos and setup script | Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription or API key; Cursor with a Cursor API key | Slack, web chat, your own cron and webhook automations | 30-day free trial, no card; billed per runtime, not per token |
| Devin | Cognition cloud VMs, or local [1] | Multi-vendor, Cognition-routed; ChatGPT plan linking on paid plans [2] | Web, desktop, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [3] | Free; Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams $80/mo + $40/seat; overage at API prices [4] |
| Codex cloud | OpenAI-hosted VMs [5] | OpenAI models; cloud needs a ChatGPT plan [6] | ChatGPT apps, CLI, IDE, Slack, GitHub, Linear [7] | In ChatGPT Plus $20/mo and up [8] |
| Cursor cloud agents | Cursor cloud VMs or self-hosted workers [9] | Billed at API prices for the chosen model; own keys chat-only [10] | Desktop, web, mobile, Slack, Teams, GitHub, Linear, API [11] | Premium $30/mo+ (X Subscription) plus API-priced usage [12] |
| Copilot cloud agent | GitHub Actions runners, 59-minute sessions [13] | Many models via GitHub; own keys not documented for it [14] | GitHub, IDEs, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [15] | Pro $10; Pro+ $39; Max $100; Business $19/user [16] |
| Jules | Google-hosted short-lived VMs [17] | Gemini only [18] | Web, GitHub label, CLI, API [19] | Free; AI Pro $19.99/mo; Ultra from $99.99/mo [20] |
| OpenHands | Local, OpenHands cloud, or self-hosted [21] | Own agent or popular CLIs; your keys [22] | GUI, CLI, API, GitHub, Slack, Jira [23] | Free (10 conversations/day hosted); Enterprise custom [24] |

## Where Devin stands in October 2026

Cognition describes Devin as an autonomous software engineer that runs in the cloud or on your machine and tests its work in its own browser. [25] It is one of the most complete products in the category, with cloud and local agents and browser testing. Devin works from its web app, Devin Desktop, the Devin CLI, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Linear and Jira, with GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket repos. [3]

The pricing model changed this year. Cognition replaced its ACU-based Core and Team plans with quota-based self-serve plans on 2026-04-14. [26] Devin's self-serve plans are Free, Pro at $20 a month, Max at $200 a month and Teams at an $80 monthly minimum plus $40 per seat; usage beyond the quota is billed at API pricing, and Enterprise is billed in ACUs. [4] The desktop editor changed too: Windsurf became Devin Desktop on 2026-06-02. [27]

People who search for Devin alternatives usually want one of three things: to stop paying a second bill for model usage they already have through Claude or ChatGPT, to pick the agent harness themselves, or to get an open-source agent they can run anywhere.

## The alternatives, ranked

Ranked for a team of 5 to 20 engineers that wants an agent working in the background on real repos, not a prototype tool.

### 1. Jiro: best if you already pay for Claude or ChatGPT

Jiro runs the coding agent you choose (Claude Code, Codex or Cursor) in an isolated cloud VM with your GitHub repos checked out and your setup script run. You talk to it in Slack or the web chat, and it opens pull requests for your team to review. It asks before it merges anything to your main branch.

Claude Code and Codex run on your own Claude subscription, ChatGPT subscription or API key, and Cursor on your Cursor API key, so you are not buying model usage twice. Jiro charges for the cloud runtime, not the tokens.

Jiro's engineering rules are public in the `public/jiro` skillset: pin down what to build before building it, write the test first, attach proof to the PR, and push back on bad ideas.

**Pick Jiro if** you want a background coding agent that works in Slack, uses the subscription you already have, and lets you switch agent harnesses without switching vendors.

### 2. OpenAI Codex cloud: best if your team lives in ChatGPT

Codex cloud runs each task in an OpenAI-hosted VM and keeps working while your laptop sleeps. [5] Codex cloud is included from ChatGPT Plus at $20 a month; Pro costs $100 to $500 a month and Business $25 per user monthly, with usage limits shared with ChatGPT. [8]

**Pick Codex cloud if** everyone already has a ChatGPT plan and OpenAI models are all you need. It runs OpenAI models only, and the GitHub and Linear integrations still sit on the legacy cloud. Codex Cloud (Legacy) still powers Code Review and the GitHub and Linear integrations, and OpenAI plans to deprecate it. [28]

### 3. Cursor cloud agents: best if your team already works in Cursor

Cursor now calls its background agents Cloud Agents. [29] Cursor cloud agents produce merge-ready PRs with screenshots, videos and logs, and open a PR in each repo they touch. [30] Cloud agents start from the Cursor desktop app, the web, iOS, Slack, Microsoft Teams, GitHub and Bitbucket comments, Linear and an API, on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps repos. [11]

**Pick Cursor cloud agents if** the editor is already your team's home. Check the pricing change first: Cursor is sold as part of The X Subscription; cloud agents need the Premium tier ($30 a month) or higher, and third-party models are billed from prepaid credit at API list price. [12]

### 4. GitHub Copilot cloud agent: best for issue-in, PR-out on GitHub

GitHub's Copilot cloud agent, formerly the Copilot coding agent, researches a repository, plans changes and implements them in an ephemeral environment powered by GitHub Actions. [31] Copilot cloud agent opens draft pull requests on its own branch and cannot approve or merge them. [32] Those are the strictest default guardrails in this list.

**Pick Copilot if** you want the agent inside GitHub itself and your tasks fit in a single session. Copilot cloud agent sessions run on GitHub Actions runners, for at most 59 minutes each, on GitHub-hosted repositories. [13]

### 5. Google Jules: best free tier

Jules allows 15 tasks a day and 3 at once on the free tier, 100 a day and 15 at once with Google AI Pro, and 300 a day and 60 at once with AI Ultra. [33] Jules runs on Google's Gemini models. [18]

**Pick Jules if** you want to try a cloud agent for free on personal projects. Paid Jules tiers are offered to personal Google accounts; Workspace users are directed to an interest form. [34]

### 6. OpenHands: best open-source option

OpenHands is an MIT-licensed open-source platform for software engineering agents. [35] OpenHands runs locally for free, as a hosted cloud service, or self-hosted in your VPC on Enterprise. [21]

**Pick OpenHands if** you need to run everything on your own infrastructure or want to read and change the agent's code.

## When Devin is still the right call

Stay with Devin if you need Microsoft Teams, Jira or GitLab today, a dedicated VPC deployment, or a vendor that handles model choice for you. Devin Enterprise offers a dedicated single-tenant VPC deployment; the agent's planning still runs in Cognition's cloud. [36] Devin's automations are also mature. Devin Automations start sessions on schedules, webhooks, and Slack, GitHub and Linear events. [37]

## What bringing your own Claude subscription saves

Devin bills usage past its quota at API prices. Jiro runs Claude Code on your own Claude credentials, so for Claude users the comparison that matters is API pricing against a flat subscription.

- Claude Opus 5.5 costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens on the Anthropic API. [38]
- Anthropic reports that across enterprise deployments Claude Code averages about $13 per developer per active day and $150 to $250 per developer per month, staying below $30 per active day for 90% of users. [39]
- Claude Max costs $100 a month for 5x the Pro plan's per-session usage or $200 a month for 20x, with limits that reset every five hours plus a weekly limit. [40]

So a typical developer's Claude Code usage is $150–250 a month at API prices, and a heavy one (under $30 a day, 21 active days) can reach about $630; a Max plan is a flat $100 or $200 per developer. Those are Anthropic's enterprise averages, not a quote, the arithmetic is ours, and Jiro's own runtime charge comes on top either way. Max has limits: heavy agent work can hit the five-hour or weekly cap, and anything beyond it is billed at API rates. Usage past a Pro or Max plan's limits can continue as extra usage billed at standard API rates. [41]

## FAQ

### What is the best alternative to Devin?

For teams that already pay for Claude or ChatGPT, Jiro: it runs Claude Code or Codex in cloud VMs on that subscription and works from Slack. For ChatGPT-only teams, Codex cloud; for GitHub-only workflows, Copilot cloud agent; for self-hosting, OpenHands.

### Is there a cheaper alternative to Devin?

Yes, if you already have a Claude or ChatGPT plan. Jiro uses that plan for model usage and charges for cloud runtime, so you avoid paying for model usage twice. Jules and OpenHands also have free tiers.

### Is Jiro the same as Devin?

No. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori. Both run coding work in cloud VMs and work from Slack, but Jiro runs the agent harness you pick on your own model subscription, while Devin runs Cognition's agent on Cognition's plans.

### What carries over if I move from Devin to Jiro?

Your GitHub repos and Slack workspace: Jiro connects to the same ones during trial setup. Devin-specific setup, such as playbooks, knowledge and automations, does not carry over; you recreate your setup script and any automations in Jiro.

Start the 30-day free trial, no card needed: https://login.norisessions.com/?signup=1&entrypoint=jiro

Or install Jiro's engineering skills into your own agent: `npx nori-skillsets install public/jiro`

15. Copilot cloud agent sessions start from GitHub issues and pull requests, GitHub Mobile, IDEs, the GitHub CLI, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Linear, Jira and Azure Boards. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/tools/about-copilot-integrations (checked 2026-10-16)

# Factory alternatives (2026): Droids vs other background coding agents

Updated 2026-10-17

> **What are the best Factory AI alternatives?**
>
> Jiro is the simplest Factory alternative: connect GitHub, Slack and your Claude or ChatGPT subscription, then ask for work in Slack and get pull requests back from an agent running in its own cloud VM. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori. Devin, Cursor cloud agents, OpenHands and GitHub Copilot cloud agent are the other main alternatives to Factory's Droids.

## Factory and its alternatives at a glance

|  | Runs where | Models and keys | Start work from | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jiro | An isolated cloud VM per conversation, with your repos and setup script | Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription or API key; Cursor with a Cursor API key | Slack, web chat, your own cron and webhook automations | 30-day free trial, no card; billed per runtime, not per token |
| Factory | Local, Factory cloud, or your machines [1] | Multi-model; own keys in CLI/desktop only [2] | App, CLI, IDE, Slack, Linear, Jira [3] | Pro $20/mo; Plus $100; Max $200; Teams $60 + $40/seat [4] |
| Devin | Cognition cloud VMs, or local [5] | Multi-vendor, Cognition-routed; ChatGPT plan linking on paid plans [6] | Web, desktop, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [7] | Free; Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams $80/mo + $40/seat; overage at API prices [8] |
| Cursor cloud agents | Cursor cloud VMs or self-hosted workers [9] | Billed at API prices for the chosen model; own keys chat-only [10] | Desktop, web, mobile, Slack, Teams, GitHub, Linear, API [11] | Premium $30/mo+ (X Subscription) plus API-priced usage [12] |
| OpenHands | Local, OpenHands cloud, or self-hosted [13] | Own agent or popular CLIs; your keys [14] | GUI, CLI, API, GitHub, Slack, Jira [15] | Free (10 conversations/day hosted); Enterprise custom [16] |
| Copilot cloud agent | GitHub Actions runners, 59-minute sessions [17] | Many models via GitHub; own keys not documented for it [18] | GitHub, IDEs, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [19] | Pro $10; Pro+ $39; Max $100; Business $19/user [20] |

## Factory in October 2026

Factory sells agent-native software development; its agents are called Droids. [21] Droids run locally in the Droid CLI and Factory App, on Factory-managed cloud Droid Computers, or on machines you register. [1] It is built for large engineering organisations, and its deployment options show it. Factory Private, launched 2026-09-18, deploys Factory into a customer's VPC, on-premises or air-gapped network. [22]

That breadth is also why smaller teams look elsewhere: it is a platform to roll out. Droids work in the Factory App, Droid CLI, headless Droid Exec and IDEs, and take delegations from Slack, Linear and Jira. [3] Its own-key support stops at the local tools. Factory routes across Anthropic, OpenAI and other models and accepts your own keys or local models in the CLI and desktop app, but not in the hosted web or mobile apps. [2]

## The alternatives, ranked

Ranked for a team that wants delegation without running a platform rollout.

### 1. Jiro: best for small teams that want it working this week

Setup is three connections: GitHub, Slack and a model provider (a Claude or ChatGPT subscription, an API key or OpenRouter). After that, each conversation gets its own cloud VM with your repos and setup script, running Claude Code or Codex (or Cursor, with a Cursor API key).

Your own subscription works in the cloud agent too, not just locally. Jiro opens pull requests for review and asks before merging to your main branch.

**Pick Jiro if** you want a coworker in Slack rather than a platform to roll out.

### 2. Devin: best for enterprise breadth without self-hosting

Cognition describes Devin as an autonomous software engineer that runs in the cloud or on your machine and tests its work in its own browser. [23] Devin works from its web app, Devin Desktop, the Devin CLI, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Linear and Jira, with GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket repos. [7]

**Pick Devin if** you want Factory-level integrations from a managed service. Devin Enterprise offers a dedicated single-tenant VPC deployment; the agent's planning still runs in Cognition's cloud. [24]

### 3. Cursor cloud agents: best for Cursor shops

Cursor cloud agents run in isolated cloud VMs with full development environments, or on self-hosted workers while Cursor runs the agent loop. [9] Cloud agents start from the Cursor desktop app, the web, iOS, Slack, Microsoft Teams, GitHub and Bitbucket comments, Linear and an API, on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps repos. [11]

**Pick Cursor if** your developers already live in the editor. Cursor is sold as part of The X Subscription; cloud agents need the Premium tier ($30 a month) or higher, and third-party models are billed from prepaid credit at API list price. [12]

### 4. OpenHands: best open-source and air-gap-friendly option

OpenHands is an MIT-licensed open-source platform for software engineering agents. [25] OpenHands runs locally for free, as a hosted cloud service, or self-hosted in your VPC on Enterprise. [13]

**Pick OpenHands if** you chose Factory for on-prem deployment but want to own the code.

### 5. GitHub Copilot cloud agent: best for GitHub-native guardrails

Copilot cloud agent opens draft pull requests on its own branch and cannot approve or merge them. [26] Copilot Pro is $10, Pro+ $39 and Max $100 a month, Business $19 and Enterprise $39 per user; Copilot Free does not include the cloud agent. [20]

**Pick Copilot if** your org already pays for Copilot Business or Enterprise.

## When Factory is the better choice

Choose Factory if you need air-gapped or on-premises deployment or Jira and Linear delegation at enterprise scale. Jiro does not offer self-hosting today.

## FAQ

### What is a simpler alternative to Factory AI?

Jiro. You install its Slack and GitHub apps, connect your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription, and ask for work in Slack. There is nothing to install on developers' machines.

### Does Factory let me use my own API keys?

Partly. Factory routes across Anthropic, OpenAI and other models and accepts your own keys or local models in the CLI and desktop app, but not in the hosted web or mobile apps. [2] Jiro uses your own subscription or key for all of its cloud work.

### Is there an open-source alternative to Factory Droids?

OpenHands. OpenHands is an MIT-licensed open-source platform for software engineering agents. [25] OpenHands runs locally for free, as a hosted cloud service, or self-hosted in your VPC on Enterprise. [13]

### Can Jiro run on-premises like Factory Private?

No. Jiro runs in Nori's cloud today. If on-premises deployment is a hard requirement, look at Factory Private or OpenHands.

## Try Jiro

Start the 30-day free trial, no card needed: https://login.norisessions.com/?signup=1&entrypoint=jiro

Or install Jiro's engineering skills into your own agent: `npx nori-skillsets install public/jiro`

# Jules alternatives (2026): cloud coding agents beyond Google's

Updated 2026-10-17

> **What are the best alternatives to Google Jules?**
>
> If you have outgrown Jules's Gemini-only models or its personal-account paid tiers, Jiro is the best alternative for teams: it runs Claude Code or Codex in cloud VMs on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription and takes requests in Slack. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori. Codex cloud, Cursor cloud agents, Copilot cloud agent, Devin and OpenHands are the other serious options.

## Jules and its alternatives at a glance

|  | Runs where | Models and keys | Start work from | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jiro | An isolated cloud VM per conversation, with your repos and setup script | Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription or API key; Cursor with a Cursor API key | Slack, web chat, your own cron and webhook automations | 30-day free trial, no card; billed per runtime, not per token |
| Jules | Google-hosted short-lived VMs [1] | Gemini only [2] | Web, GitHub label, CLI, API [3] | Free; AI Pro $19.99/mo; Ultra from $99.99/mo [4] |
| Codex cloud | OpenAI-hosted VMs [5] | OpenAI models; cloud needs a ChatGPT plan [6] | ChatGPT apps, CLI, IDE, Slack, GitHub, Linear [7] | In ChatGPT Plus $20/mo and up [8] |
| Cursor cloud agents | Cursor cloud VMs or self-hosted workers [9] | Billed at API prices for the chosen model; own keys chat-only [10] | Desktop, web, mobile, Slack, Teams, GitHub, Linear, API [11] | Premium $30/mo+ (X Subscription) plus API-priced usage [12] |
| Copilot cloud agent | GitHub Actions runners, 59-minute sessions [13] | Many models via GitHub; own keys not documented for it [14] | GitHub, IDEs, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [15] | Pro $10; Pro+ $39; Max $100; Business $19/user [16] |
| Devin | Cognition cloud VMs, or local [17] | Multi-vendor, Cognition-routed; ChatGPT plan linking on paid plans [18] | Web, desktop, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [19] | Free; Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams $80/mo + $40/seat; overage at API prices [20] |
| OpenHands | Local, OpenHands cloud, or self-hosted [21] | Own agent or popular CLIs; your keys [22] | GUI, CLI, API, GitHub, Slack, Jira [23] | Free (10 conversations/day hosted); Enterprise custom [24] |

## What Jules does well, and where teams hit its limits

Google's Jules runs each task inside a short-lived VM with common toolchains and Docker installed. [1] Jules allows 15 tasks a day and 3 at once on the free tier, 100 a day and 15 at once with Google AI Pro, and 300 a day and 60 at once with AI Ultra. [25] That free tier is generous, and it is a good way to see whether a cloud agent fits your work at all.

Teams run into three limits. Jules runs on Google's Gemini models. [2] Paid Jules tiers are offered to personal Google accounts; Workspace users are directed to an interest form. [26] And work starts from the web app, GitHub, the CLI or the API rather than the chat tool your team already uses. Jules takes work from its web app, GitHub issues labelled jules, the Jules Tools CLI and the Jules API. [3]

## The alternatives, ranked

Ranked for a small engineering team that wants a cloud coding agent it can hand real tickets to.

### 1. Jiro: best for teams that want model choice and Slack

Jiro gives each conversation its own cloud VM with your GitHub repos and setup script, then runs the agent you pick: Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription, an API key or OpenRouter, or Cursor on a Cursor key.

Your team asks for work by mentioning Jiro in Slack or in the web chat. It opens pull requests for review and asks before merging to your main branch. Recurring work runs on cron or webhook automations you set up.

**Pick Jiro if** Jules's single model family or personal-account paid tiers are what is holding you back.

### 2. OpenAI Codex cloud: the closest one-vendor equivalent

Codex cloud runs each task in an OpenAI-hosted VM and keeps working while your laptop sleeps. [5] Codex cloud is included from ChatGPT Plus at $20 a month; Pro costs $100 to $500 a month and Business $25 per user monthly, with usage limits shared with ChatGPT. [8] It covers more surfaces than Jules, including Slack. Codex requests in Slack now start with @ChatGPT instead of @Codex. [27]

**Pick Codex cloud if** your team is standardised on ChatGPT.

### 3. Cursor cloud agents: best inside the Cursor editor

Cursor cloud agents run in isolated cloud VMs with full development environments, or on self-hosted workers while Cursor runs the agent loop. [9] Cursor cloud agents produce merge-ready PRs with screenshots, videos and logs, and open a PR in each repo they touch. [28]

**Pick Cursor if** your developers already use it daily and the new plan structure works for you. Cursor is sold as part of The X Subscription; cloud agents need the Premium tier ($30 a month) or higher, and third-party models are billed from prepaid credit at API list price. [12]

### 4. GitHub Copilot cloud agent: best if the work starts as GitHub issues

GitHub's Copilot cloud agent, formerly the Copilot coding agent, researches a repository, plans changes and implements them in an ephemeral environment powered by GitHub Actions. [29] Copilot cloud agent opens draft pull requests on its own branch and cannot approve or merge them. [30]

**Pick Copilot if** you want the agent built into GitHub and short sessions are enough. Copilot cloud agent sessions run on GitHub Actions runners, for at most 59 minutes each, on GitHub-hosted repositories. [13]

### 5. Devin: best fully managed option

Cognition describes Devin as an autonomous software engineer that runs in the cloud or on your machine and tests its work in its own browser. [31] Devin works from its web app, Devin Desktop, the Devin CLI, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Linear and Jira, with GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket repos. [19]

**Pick Devin if** you want one vendor to handle the agent, models and integrations and are fine with quota-based plans. Devin's self-serve plans are Free, Pro at $20 a month, Max at $200 a month and Teams at an $80 monthly minimum plus $40 per seat; usage beyond the quota is billed at API pricing, and Enterprise is billed in ACUs. [20]

### 6. OpenHands: best for self-hosting

OpenHands is an MIT-licensed open-source platform for software engineering agents. [32] OpenHands' hosted Individual tier is free for one user with 10 conversations a day; local use is free and Enterprise is custom. [24]

**Pick OpenHands if** you need the agent on your own machines.

## When to stay on Jules

Stay on Jules if you are an individual developer on a personal Google account, you are happy with Gemini models, and the free or AI Pro limits cover your volume. It also has recurring work built in. Jules can run Scheduled Tasks on a recurring basis. [33]

## FAQ

### What is the best alternative to Google Jules?

For teams, Jiro: it runs Claude Code or Codex in cloud VMs on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription and works from Slack. For ChatGPT users, Codex cloud is the closest equivalent.

### Can I use Jules with a Google Workspace account?

Not on the paid tiers yet. Paid Jules tiers are offered to personal Google accounts; Workspace users are directed to an interest form. [26]

### Which models can I use with Jiro?

Jiro's setup recommends a Claude or ChatGPT subscription, or an API key for either, and also accepts OpenRouter and custom endpoints. Jiro runs Claude Code or Codex with them, and Cursor with a Cursor API key.

### Is Jiro made by Google?

No. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori, an independent company.

## Try Jiro

Start the 30-day free trial, no card needed: https://login.norisessions.com/?signup=1&entrypoint=jiro

Or install Jiro's engineering skills into your own agent: `npx nori-skillsets install public/jiro`

12. Cursor is sold as part of The X Subscription; cloud agents need the Premium tier ($30 a month) or higher, and third-party models are billed from prepaid credit at API list price. Source: https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing.md (checked 2026-10-16)
13. Copilot cloud agent sessions run on GitHub Actions runners, for at most 59 minutes each, on GitHub-hosted repositories. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/cloud-agent/customize-the-agent-environment (checked 2026-10-16)
14. The cloud agent offers Auto plus Claude, Gemini, GPT and Grok models; bring-your-own-key is documented for Copilot Chat, CLI and IDEs, not for the cloud agent. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/models/bring-your-own-key (checked 2026-10-16)
15. Copilot cloud agent sessions start from GitHub issues and pull requests, GitHub Mobile, IDEs, the GitHub CLI, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Linear, Jira and Azure Boards. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/tools/about-copilot-integrations (checked 2026-10-16)
16. Copilot Pro is $10, Pro+ $39 and Max $100 a month, Business $19 and Enterprise $39 per user; Copilot Free does not include the cloud agent. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/get-started/plans (checked 2026-10-16)
17. Devin Cloud runs each session in its own VM; Devin CLI and Devin Desktop run locally. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/llms.txt (checked 2026-10-16)
18. Devin uses models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google plus Cognition's own SWE models, picked by an Adaptive router; Pro, Max and Teams users can link a ChatGPT plan for the GPT share of usage. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/chatgpt.md (checked 2026-10-16)
19. Devin works from its web app, Devin Desktop, the Devin CLI, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Linear and Jira, with GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket repos. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/llms.txt (checked 2026-10-16)
20. Devin's self-serve plans are Free, Pro at $20 a month, Max at $200 a month and Teams at an $80 monthly minimum plus $40 per seat; usage beyond the quota is billed at API pricing, and Enterprise is billed in ACUs. Source: https://devin.ai/pricing (checked 2026-10-16)
21. OpenHands runs locally for free, as a hosted cloud service, or self-hosted in your VPC on Enterprise. Source: https://openhands.dev/pricing (checked 2026-10-16)
22. OpenHands runs its own agent or Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, on your own model keys or at-cost models. Source: https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands (checked 2026-10-16)
23. OpenHands works from its GUI, CLI, SDK and API, from GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket, and from Slack and Jira. Source: https://openhands.dev/pricing (checked 2026-10-16)
24. OpenHands' hosted Individual tier is free for one user with 10 conversations a day; local use is free and Enterprise is custom. Source: https://openhands.dev/pricing (checked 2026-10-16)
25. Jules allows 15 tasks a day and 3 at once on the free tier, 100 a day and 15 at once with Google AI Pro, and 300 a day and 60 at once with AI Ultra. Source: https://jules.google/docs/usage-limits (checked 2026-10-16)
26. Paid Jules tiers are offered to personal Google accounts; Workspace users are directed to an interest form. Source: https://jules.google/docs/usage-limits (checked 2026-10-16)

# Kiro alternatives (2026): other AI coding agents to Amazon's Kiro

Updated 2026-10-17

> **What are the best alternatives to Amazon Kiro?**
>
> Jiro is the best Kiro alternative if you want an agent your team works with in Slack, running Claude Code or Codex in cloud VMs on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription instead of Kiro credits. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori. It is not a version of Amazon's Kiro. Cursor cloud agents, GitHub Copilot cloud agent, Claude Code on the web, Codex cloud and Devin are the other main options.

## Kiro and the alternatives at a glance

|  | Runs where | Models and keys | Start work from | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jiro | An isolated cloud VM per conversation, with your repos and setup script | Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription or API key; Cursor with a Cursor API key | Slack, web chat, your own cron and webhook automations | 30-day free trial, no card; billed per runtime, not per token |
| Kiro | AWS sandbox (us-east-1) or local [1] | Claude, GPT and open models via Kiro credits [2] | IDE, CLI, web, iOS; GitHub and GitLab [3] | Free 50 credits; Pro $20; Pro+ $40; Pro Max $100; Power $200 [4] |
| Cursor cloud agents | Cursor cloud VMs or self-hosted workers [5] | Billed at API prices for the chosen model; own keys chat-only [6] | Desktop, web, mobile, Slack, Teams, GitHub, Linear, API [7] | Premium $30/mo+ (X Subscription) plus API-priced usage [8] |
| Copilot cloud agent | GitHub Actions runners, 59-minute sessions [9] | Many models via GitHub; own keys not documented for it [10] | GitHub, IDEs, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [11] | Pro $10; Pro+ $39; Max $100; Business $19/user [12] |
| Claude Code on the web | Anthropic-managed VMs [13] | Claude models; Anthropic account required [14] | Web, mobile, desktop, terminal [15] | In Pro $20/mo, Max $100+/mo, Team seats [16] |
| Codex cloud | OpenAI-hosted VMs [17] | OpenAI models; cloud needs a ChatGPT plan [18] | ChatGPT apps, CLI, IDE, Slack, GitHub, Linear [19] | In ChatGPT Plus $20/mo and up [20] |
| Devin | Cognition cloud VMs, or local [21] | Multi-vendor, Cognition-routed; ChatGPT plan linking on paid plans [22] | Web, desktop, CLI, Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira [23] | Free; Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams $80/mo + $40/seat; overage at API prices [24] |

## Kiro in October 2026

Kiro is Amazon's AI coding agent, built around one agent harness across the IDE, CLI, web and mobile, with spec-driven development as its signature workflow. [25] Kiro Web launched in preview on 2026-05-18 with an Autonomous toggle, folding in the Kiro autonomous agent announced at re:Invent 2025. [26] Kiro cloud sessions run in an AWS-managed sandbox in us-east-1, up to 10 at a time, with no separate compute charge; the IDE and CLI also run locally. [1]

Its pricing is transparent and its free tier is real. Kiro's plans are Free (50 credits a month), Pro at $20, Pro+ at $40, Pro Max at $100 and Power at $200 a month, with extra credits at $0.04 each; Kiro Web needs a paid plan. [4] What pushes people to alternatives is mostly model access: Kiro offers Claude, GPT-5.6 and open-weight models through its own credits, and its terms prohibit routing requests through third-party harnesses. [2]

## The alternatives, ranked

Ranked for teams that want background work on their repos rather than a new IDE.

### 1. Jiro: best for Slack and your own subscription

Jiro gives each conversation an isolated cloud VM with your GitHub repos and setup script, and runs Claude Code or Codex on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription, an API key or OpenRouter, or Cursor with a Cursor API key. There are no credits to buy for model usage; Jiro bills for the runtime.

Your team mentions Jiro in Slack or uses the web chat, and gets pull requests back for review. Jiro asks before merging to your main branch.

**Pick Jiro if** you want a teammate in Slack rather than an IDE, and want to keep paying for models through your existing plan.

### 2. Cursor cloud agents: best IDE-plus-cloud alternative

Cursor cloud agents run in isolated cloud VMs with full development environments, or on self-hosted workers while Cursor runs the agent loop. [5] Cursor cloud agents produce merge-ready PRs with screenshots, videos and logs, and open a PR in each repo they touch. [27]

**Pick Cursor if** you chose Kiro for the IDE and want a similar local-plus-cloud setup. Cursor is sold as part of The X Subscription; cloud agents need the Premium tier ($30 a month) or higher, and third-party models are billed from prepaid credit at API list price. [8]

### 3. GitHub Copilot cloud agent: best for issue-driven work

GitHub's Copilot cloud agent, formerly the Copilot coding agent, researches a repository, plans changes and implements them in an ephemeral environment powered by GitHub Actions. [28] Copilot cloud agent opens draft pull requests on its own branch and cannot approve or merge them. [29]

**Pick Copilot if** you liked Kiro's label-an-issue flow and want it native to GitHub.

### 4. Claude Code on the web: best for Claude subscribers

A Claude Code cloud session runs on Anthropic-managed infrastructure (by default a 4 vCPU, 16 GB VM) and keeps running after you close your laptop. [13] Claude Code is included in Claude Pro ($20 a month), Max (from $100 a month) and Team and Enterprise seats, with no separate charge for the cloud VM; the Free plan has no Claude Code. [16]

**Pick it if** you want Claude models on your own Claude plan.

### 5. OpenAI Codex cloud: best for ChatGPT subscribers

Codex cloud runs each task in an OpenAI-hosted VM and keeps working while your laptop sleeps. [17] Codex cloud is included from ChatGPT Plus at $20 a month; Pro costs $100 to $500 a month and Business $25 per user monthly, with usage limits shared with ChatGPT. [20]

**Pick Codex cloud if** your team is on ChatGPT.

### 6. Devin: best managed enterprise option

Cognition describes Devin as an autonomous software engineer that runs in the cloud or on your machine and tests its work in its own browser. [30] Devin Enterprise offers a dedicated single-tenant VPC deployment; the agent's planning still runs in Cognition's cloud. [31]

**Pick Devin if** you want broad enterprise integrations from one vendor.

## When Kiro is the right choice

Choose Kiro if you want spec-driven development in a polished IDE, or a free tier to start with. Kiro also leaves merging to you, which is the right default. Kiro opens pull requests from a kiro label or /kiro comment on a GitHub issue and never merges changes automatically. [32]

## FAQ

### Is Jiro the same as Kiro?

No. Jiro is a background coding agent by Nori, an independent company. Kiro is Amazon's AI coding agent and IDE. The names are one letter apart; the products and companies are unrelated.

### What is the best free Kiro alternative?

Google Jules and OpenHands have free tiers. Jules allows 15 tasks a day and 3 at once on the free tier, 100 a day and 15 at once with Google AI Pro, and 300 a day and 60 at once with AI Ultra. [33] OpenHands' hosted Individual tier is free for one user with 10 conversations a day; local use is free and Enterprise is custom. [34] Jiro has a 30-day free trial with no card.

### Can I use my own Claude subscription instead of Kiro credits?

Kiro sells model access through its own credits. Kiro offers Claude, GPT-5.6 and open-weight models through its own credits, and its terms prohibit routing requests through third-party harnesses. [2] With Jiro, Claude Code runs on your own Claude subscription or API key.

## Try Jiro

Start the 30-day free trial, no card needed: https://login.norisessions.com/?signup=1&entrypoint=jiro

Or install Jiro's engineering skills into your own agent: `npx nori-skillsets install public/jiro`
